findings.message: The "*" (keep) branch only looks up existingCred.Env[u] using the new URL. The UI renames the credential key from oldUrl to newUrl with value "*" to request a transfer, but the backend never looks up the old URL's token, so the token is silently dropped. An admin edits the source https://gitlab.com/org/repo (token stored) to https://gitlab.com/org/repo/dev and leaves the token field empty. The UI sends {".../repo/dev": "*"}. existingCred.Env has no ".../repo/dev" key, and the old URL is no longer active, so newTokens is empty and the credential is deleted. The next sync of the private repo fails with an auth error.

Update rewrites scheme-less SourceURLs to https://..., but the SourceURLCredentials keys are not normalized. activeURLs then no longer contains the client's key, so the newly entered token is skipped by `if !active { continue }`. In the dialog an admin enters "github.com/acme/private-catalog" with a PAT. SourceURLs becomes ["https://github.com/acme/private-catalog"] while the credential key stays "github.com/acme/private-catalog". The token is discarded without any error, and the sync fails because the repo is private.

isGitRepoURL now treats every gitlab.com URL as a git repo. Raw-file catalog URLs that used to be fetched over HTTP are now sent to parseGitURL, which takes the trailing path as a branch name. An existing source https://gitlab.com/org/repo/-/raw/main/catalog.yaml now produces the branch "-/raw/main/catalog.yaml". validateBranchName rejects it because of the leading "-", so a catalog that used to sync now fails every time.

sizeLimitedFS is shared by the .git storer (chrooted) and the worktree, so the 100 MB budget is charged for both the packfile and the checked-out files. A repository whose real size is well under 100 MB can still fail. A repo with a 55 MB packfile that expands to 50 MB of checked-out files writes about 105 MB in total. The clone aborts with "repository is too large (limit: 100 MB)", even though GitHub reports the repo size as 55 MB, which is under the limit.

resolveToken only falls back to GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN when the URL exactly matches the hard-coded default catalog URL. Existing private GitHub catalogs that relied on the env token, and any catalog URL with a branch suffix or a custom default path, now clone and call the API without authentication. A deployment configured GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN to sync https://github.com/acme/private-catalog. After upgrading, the size check gets a 404 or rate-limit 403 from the unauthenticated GitHub API and the sync fails, with no migration path other than re-entering a per-URL token.
